entities.name: Cholera
entities.description: Acute, life-threatening diarrhoeal infection caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae (serogroups O1 and O139), characterized by abrupt onset of profuse, painless secretory watery diarrhea, severe dehydration, and rapid hypovolemic shock within hours.

entities.name: Fecally Contaminated Drinking Water and Compromised WASH Infrastructure
entities.description: Primary fecal-oral transmission vehicle, prevalent during humanitarian crises, refugee displacement, flooding, or municipal water and sewage system collapse.

entities.name: Raw or Undercooked Shellfish from Brackish Estuarine Waters
entities.description: Marine reservoir exposure where Vibrio cholerae colonizes chitinous surfaces of zooplankton (copepods) and shellfish in warm coastal and estuarine aquatic ecosystems (>15-20°C).

entities.name: Blood Group O Host Susceptibility
entities.description: Inherent host immunogenetic risk factor strongly predisposing individuals to severe cholera gravis and life-threatening dehydration upon Vibrio cholerae exposure.

entities.name: Vibrio cholerae Serogroups O1 and O139
entities.description: Comma-shaped, highly motile, oxidase-positive Gram-negative bacilli; epidemic cholera is caused exclusively by serogroup O1 (biotypes Classical and El Tor; serotypes Inaba, Ogawa, Hikojima) and serogroup O139 Bengal.

entities.name: Cholera Enterotoxin AB5 Subunit Complex
entities.description: Potent protein enterotoxin consisting of an enzymatically active A subunit and five B receptor-binding subunits, responsible for catastrophic intestinal fluid and electrolyte hypersecretion.

entities.name: Painless Voluminous Rice-Water Diarrhea
entities.description: Pathognomonic triage physical hallmark presenting as explosive, effortless, translucent grayish-white watery stool with suspended mucus flecks and a fishy odor, lacking fecal matter, blood, or pus, purging 500-1000 mL/hour.

entities.name: Severe Hypovolemic Shock with Washerwoman Wrinkled Skin and Hollow Orbits
entities.description: Life-threatening triage sign of cholera gravis with >10% body weight fluid deficit, manifesting with sunken eyes, deeply shriveled wrinkled fingers ('washerwoman's hands'), absent radial pulse, skin pinch retraction >2 seconds, and hoarse whispering voice (vox cholerica).

entities.name: Effortless Non-Bilious Watery Vomiting
entities.description: Sudden projectile, non-bilious clear watery vomiting occurring soon after diarrhea onset without preceding nausea or retching, accelerating dehydration.

entities.name: Excruciating Calf and Abdominal Muscle Cramps
entities.description: Severe painful tonic spasms primarily involving the gastrocnemius, thigh, and abdominal wall musculature, caused by profound acute hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and base loss.

entities.name: Rapid Darting Shooting-Star Motility on Darkfield Stool Microscopy
entities.description: Point-of-care microscopic finding in fresh rice-water stool demonstrating rapidly darting vibrios with characteristic scintillating motility that is instantly arrested by specific O1/O139 antiserum.

entities.name: Severe Hemoconcentration and Stress Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: Admission CBC showing markedly elevated hematocrit (50-60%) and hemoglobin (>18-20 g/dL) reflecting profound plasma volume depletion, accompanied by stress leukocytosis (WBC 15,000-25,000/µL) with normal platelets.

entities.name: Profound Metabolic Acidosis with Collapsed Serum Bicarbonate
entities.description: Admission chemistry and blood gas pattern with serum bicarbonate collapsing to <8-12 mEq/L and pH <7.15-7.25 due to massive intestinal bicarbonate loss (fecal [HCO3-] 40-50 mEq/L) and lactic acidosis, provoking compensatory Kussmaul respiration.

entities.name: Prerenal Azotemia with BUN to Creatinine Ratio Exceeding 20 to 1
entities.description: Severe acute kidney injury pattern on admission metabolic panel with elevated BUN and serum creatinine, marked oliguria or anuria, and BUN:creatinine ratio >20:1 driven by renal hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Acellular Fecal Smear Lacking Pus Cells and Erythrocytes
entities.description: Admission point-of-care stool microscopy demonstrating complete absence of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (pus cells) and red blood cells, confirming a non-invasive secretory pathology.

entities.name: Inferior Vena Cava Complete Collapse on Bedside Ultrasound
entities.description: Admission POCUS examination demonstrating slit-like, completely collapsed inferior vena cava with >50% inspiratory collapsibility and hyperperistaltic fluid-distended small bowel loops without bowel wall thickening.

entities.name: Point-of-Care Cholera O1 and O139 Dipstick Antigen Test
entities.description: Rapid immunochromatographic dipstick testing of fresh stool providing immediate triage identification of Vibrio cholerae O1 and O139 lipopolysaccharide antigens at admission.

entities.name: High Continuous Fever Exceeding 39°C
entities.description: High continuous pyrexia (>39°C) in an adult patient at presentation, characteristic of invasive systemic or enteric infections but fundamentally atypical of cholera.

entities.name: Gross Hematochezia Melena or Stool Pus Cells
entities.description: Presence of macroscopic red blood, dark black melenic stool, or sheets of fecal polymorphonuclear neutrophils on microscopic smear indicating mucosal ulceration.

entities.name: Chronic Diarrheal Duration Exceeding 7 Days
entities.description: Diarrheal illness persisting or recurring for more than one week, incompatible with the acute explosive hyper-voluminous course of cholera.

entities.name: Severe Tenesmus and Low-Volume Colicky Stools
entities.description: Intense painful rectal straining (tenesmus) accompanied by painful small-volume mucoid evacuations, pathognomonic of invasive rectosigmoid colitis.

entities.name: Bacillary Dysentery
entities.description: Acute invasive bacterial infection of the colon caused by Shigella species, presenting with high fever, severe colicky abdominal cramps, tenesmus, and bloody mucoid stools.

entities.name: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli Gastroenteritis
entities.description: Common cause of traveler's watery diarrhea caused by heat-labile (LT) and/or heat-stable (ST) enterotoxins, resulting in self-limited watery stools.

entities.name: Amoebic Dysentery
entities.description: Invasive colonic protozoan infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, causing subacute bloody diarrhea and discrete ulcerations.

entities.name: Viral Gastroenteritis
entities.description: Acute viral intestinal infection caused by Rotavirus or Norovirus, characterized by prominent antecedent nausea, vomiting preceding diarrhea, and low-grade fever.

entities.name: Intravenous Ringer's Lactate Resuscitation
entities.description: First-line crystalloid resuscitation solution providing balanced electrolytes and lactate substrate to rapidly reverse hypovolemic shock, restore arterial pressure, and buffer severe metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Reduced-Osmolarity Oral Rehydration Solution
entities.description: Standard WHO oral electrolyte solution utilizing intact SGLT-1 intestinal sodium-glucose cotransport to drive passive mucosal water absorption, matching ongoing stool volume loss.

entities.name: Single-Dose Oral Doxycycline or Azithromycin Regimen
entities.description: Adjunctive single-dose antimicrobial therapy (Doxycycline 300 mg or Azithromycin 1 g) administered following initial rehydration to eradicate Vibrio carriage and curb purging volume.

entities.name: Adjunctive Oral Zinc Therapy in Pediatric Cholera
entities.description: Adjunctive micronutrient therapy (20 mg/day for 10-14 days) in children under 5 years, accelerating mucosal regeneration and reducing diarrhea duration.

entities.name: Antibiotic Monotherapy Without Aggressive Fluid Resuscitation
entities.description: Lethal clinical pitfall of administering antibiotics alone without immediate, aggressive intravenous and oral fluid replacement, which fails to prevent cardiovascular collapse.

relationships.target: Fecally Contaminated Drinking Water and Compromised WASH Infrastructure
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, fecal-oral transmission, contaminated water, WASH breakdown, environmental risk
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Ingestion of municipal or surface water contaminated with human fecal matter is the predominant transmission route driving explosive cholera outbreaks.

relationships.target: Raw or Undercooked Shellfish from Brackish Estuarine Waters
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, marine reservoir, undercooked shellfish, estuarine ecosystem
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Ingestion of raw or insufficiently cooked oysters, crabs, or other shellfish harvested from warm, brackish estuarine waters serves as an established vehicle for sporadic and epidemic cholera.

relationships.target: Blood Group O Host Susceptibility
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, host genetic susceptibility, blood group O, severe disease risk
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Individuals with blood group O possess heightened clinical vulnerability to developing severe, life-threatening dehydration (cholera gravis) following Vibrio cholerae exposure.

relationships.target: Vibrio cholerae Serogroups O1 and O139
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative organism, comma bacillus, O1 and O139 serogroups
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Cholera is caused by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae serogroup O1 (Classical or El Tor biotypes) or serogroup O139, which colonize the small intestinal mucosa.

relationships.target: Cholera Enterotoxin AB5 Subunit Complex
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, cholera toxin, AB5 enterotoxin, adenylate cyclase activation
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates the Gs-alpha regulatory protein in small intestinal enterocytes, permanently activating adenylate cyclase and driving massive intracellular cAMP accumulation with active chloride, bicarbonate, and water secretion.

relationships.target: Painless Voluminous Rice-Water Diarrhea
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, rice-water stool, high purging rate
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The abrupt appearance of copious, non-bloody, translucent rice-water stool purging at rates of up to 1 L/hour without abdominal pain or tenesmus is the pathognomonic hallmark of severe cholera.

relationships.target: Severe Hypovolemic Shock with Washerwoman Wrinkled Skin and Hollow Orbits
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, cholera gravis, washerwoman hands, hypovolemic shock
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Critical intravascular collapse featuring washerwoman wrinkled fingertips, hollow eyes, impalpable radial pulse, and vox cholerica reflects rapid loss of >10% body fluid volume within hours.

relationships.target: Effortless Non-Bilious Watery Vomiting
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, projectile vomiting, painless fluid loss, admission hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Painless, effortless clear watery vomiting emerges abruptly following the onset of watery purging, drastically exacerbating acute volume depletion.

relationships.target: Excruciating Calf and Abdominal Muscle Cramps
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, severe muscle cramps, hypokalemic spasm, calf cramps
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Excruciating spasms of the calf muscles and abdominal wall develop rapidly at triage due to catastrophic fecal depletion of potassium, magnesium, and bicarbonate.

relationships.target: Rapid Darting Shooting-Star Motility on Darkfield Stool Microscopy
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, point of care, shooting-star motility, darkfield microscopy
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Direct darkfield examination of fresh rice-water stool reveals the classic scintillating shooting-star motility of Vibrio cholerae, confirmed at triage by immediate immobilization with anti-O1/O139 antiserum.

relationships.target: Severe Hemoconcentration and Stress Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, admission CBC, hemoconcentration, elevated hematocrit
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Markedly contracted intravascular volume produces severe hemoconcentration with hematocrit reaching 50-60% and secondary catecholamine-mediated neutrophilic leukocytosis on admission CBC.

relationships.target: Profound Metabolic Acidosis with Collapsed Serum Bicarbonate
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, metabolic acidosis, base deficit, Kussmaul breathing
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Massive stool bicarbonate loss leads to severe metabolic acidosis with serum bicarbonate collapsing below 12 mEq/L and compensatory deep Kussmaul breathing on arrival.

relationships.target: Prerenal Azotemia with BUN to Creatinine Ratio Exceeding 20 to 1
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, prerenal acute kidney injury, elevated BUN creatinine ratio
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Acute prerenal azotemia with a BUN to creatinine ratio >20:1 develops rapidly at admission as severe dehydration causes renal hypoperfusion and oliguria.

relationships.target: Acellular Fecal Smear Lacking Pus Cells and Erythrocytes
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, stool smear, absent fecal leukocytes, acellular stool
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Microscopic evaluation of rice-water stool reveals an acellular smear devoid of fecal leukocytes and erythrocytes, establishing an enterotoxin-driven non-invasive secretory process.

relationships.target: Inferior Vena Cava Complete Collapse on Bedside Ultrasound
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, imaging hallmark, POCUS, collapsed IVC, hyperperistaltic bowel
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside POCUS ultrasound confirms critical intravascular hypovolemia via an unvisualized or fully collapsing inferior vena cava and reveals fluid-filled hyperactive small bowel loops without wall thickening.

relationships.target: Point-of-Care Cholera O1 and O139 Dipstick Antigen Test
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, lab hallmark, point of care, rapid diagnostic test, RDT antigen
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid immunochromatographic dipstick testing of fresh stool provides immediate point-of-care identification of Vibrio cholerae O1 and O139 lipopolysaccharide antigens at hospital admission.

relationships.target: High Continuous Fever Exceeding 39°C
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, high fever
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of high continuous fever (>39°C) at admission strongly rules out uncomplicated cholera, which is afebrile or presents with hypothermia in shock.

relationships.target: Gross Hematochezia Melena or Stool Pus Cells
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, bloody stool, fecal leukocytes
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] The presence of gross blood, melena, or fecal pus cells on admission microscopy rules out cholera, signaling an invasive mucosal enteritis such as shigellosis or amoebiasis.

relationships.target: Chronic Diarrheal Duration Exceeding 7 Days
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, chronic diarrhea timeline
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A diarrheal duration of greater than 7 days rules out acute cholera, which presents with hyperacute onset (hours to days) and completes its course within 2 to 6 days.

relationships.target: Severe Tenesmus and Low-Volume Colicky Stools
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, tenesmus, low volume stool
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Painful tenesmus with small-volume colicky evacuations rules out cholera, which is characterized by painless, effortless, massive-volume fluid purging.

relationships.target: Bacillary Dysentery
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, Shigella, dysentery
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Bacillary dysentery presents with high fever (>39°C), severe colicky abdominal cramps, tenesmus, and small-volume bloody stools filled with pus cells; cholera presents with painless, massive non-bloody rice-water diarrhea, normal temperature, and an acellular stool smear.

relationships.target: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli Gastroenteritis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, ETEC, traveler's diarrhea
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] ETEC produces modest self-limiting diarrhea (3-5 stools/day, rarely exceeding 1-2 L/day) without severe dehydration; cholera produces catastrophic multi-liter purging (>500-1000 mL/hr, 10-20 L/day), washerwoman skin, and rapid hypovolemic shock.

relationships.target: Amoebic Dysentery
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, Entamoeba histolytica, amoebiasis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Amoebic dysentery has an insidious subacute onset over 1-3 weeks with localized right-lower-quadrant tenderness and low-volume bloody stools with erythrophagocytic trophozoites; cholera has an explosive onset over hours with painless massive rice-water purging.

relationships.target: Viral Gastroenteritis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, Rotavirus, Norovirus
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Viral gastroenteritis typically features antecedent nausea, persistent vomiting prior to diarrhea, low-grade fever, and low to moderate stool purging volumes; cholera presents with abrupt effortless diarrhea followed by vomiting, non-bloody rice-water effluent, and massive purging volumes.

relationships.target: Intravenous Ringer's Lactate Resuscitation
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, fluid resuscitation, Ringer's lactate, hypovolemic shock reversal
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Rapid intravenous infusion of Ringer's lactate (100 mL/kg, with 30 mL/kg within 30 minutes in adults) restores peripheral pulses and normalizes blood pressure within 1-2 hours while lactate metabolizes to correct profound acidosis.

relationships.target: Reduced-Osmolarity Oral Rehydration Solution
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, oral rehydration solution, WHO ORS, sodium-glucose cotransport
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Reduced-osmolarity WHO-ORS restores and maintains hydration by exploiting intact intestinal sodium-glucose cotransport even during active enterotoxin-mediated secretion, dramatically reducing mortality to <1%.

relationships.target: Single-Dose Oral Doxycycline or Azithromycin Regimen
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, antimicrobial therapy, single-dose doxycycline, azithromycin, volume reduction
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Single-dose oral doxycycline (300 mg) or azithromycin (1 g) administered after initial fluid stabilization halves diarrheal stool output and shortens Vibrio cholerae fecal excretion to 24-48 hours.

relationships.target: Adjunctive Oral Zinc Therapy in Pediatric Cholera
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, pediatric zinc supplementation, mucosal regeneration, diarrhea reduction
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Adjunctive oral zinc supplementation (20 mg/day for 10-14 days) in children under 5 years significantly reduces the total duration and volume of diarrheal stool output.

relationships.target: Antibiotic Monotherapy Without Aggressive Fluid Resuscitation
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, treatment failure, antibiotic monotherapy, fatal dehydration
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Cholera fails to respond to antimicrobial therapy alone without aggressive fluid resuscitation, resulting in fatal hypovolemic shock and renal shutdown within hours despite bacterial eradication.
